extracted.intended_audience: writers, readers, and prospective contributors to The Paris Review
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial mission and selection standards for The Paris Review, describing what kinds of work the magazine prioritizes (fiction, poetry, interviews) and the qualities it seeks in contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on original creative work (fiction & poetry)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Paris Review hopes to emphasize creative work—fiction and poetry...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Review prioritizes original creative writing (fiction and poetry) over criticism; criticism is not excluded but should not dominate the magazine and is intended to be moved "somewhere near the back of the book." This signals a preference for submissions of creative pieces rather than critical essays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for high-quality writers and poets
rubrics_metrics.description: The Review "should welcome these people into its pages: the good writers and good poets... So long as they're good."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality of writing is a primary selection criterion; the magazine seeks strong literary craftsmanship and voice. The phrasing implies editorial taste as a gatekeeping principle: excellence in prose or poetry is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of polemical/agitation-driven work
rubrics_metrics.description: The Review says it should welcome "the non-drumbeaters and non-axe-grinders."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine disfavors work that is primarily polemical, agitational, or driven by 'drumbeating'—i.e., overtly partisan or hammering an agenda. Preference is for subtler, literary aims rather than agitprop or relentless polemic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest in introducing important or consequential writers/works
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically the Review "has introduced the important writers of the day" and first published early work by many now-notable authors (examples listed: Adrienne Rich, Philip Roth, Italo Calvino, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Review looks for work that may have lasting literary significance or come from emerging writers who could become important. The historical examples function as implicit guidance about the level and kind of originality, quality, and distinctiveness the magazine values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-form, revealing author interviews (Writers at Work)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Review’s Writers at Work interview series "offers authors a rare opportunity to discuss their life and art at length; they have responded with some of the most revealing self-portraits in literature."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For interviews, the magazine favors in-depth, long-form conversations where authors discuss their life and craft at length, producing revealing, reflective material rather than short promotional pieces or superficial Q&A.
